This notebook takes Wilcoxon test statistics and dPSI values for query and reference groups chosen in `scripts/06-diffsplice_calculation.R` as input. After filtering for splice events with user-defined padj and dPSI thresholds, this notebook performs over-representation analysis (ORA) on the parent genes of the filtered splice events.

Caveats:

- The input to this notebook is currently the AML (stranded) vs. Whole Blood (unstranded) diffsplice results so doesn't reflect the biological comparison we want to make for the manuscript.

Gene sets used in this analysis fall under two categories:

Category 1: Genes documented to be differentially spliced when splicing factors are mutated in blood cancers

- Custom gene set: u2af1_leuk_diffsplice_genes - list of 16 genes differentially spliced in U2AF1 mutant vs. WT cells in AMLCG, Beat AML datasets, Okeyo-Owuor et al. (Table S14 of [Bamopoulos](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41375-020-0839-4#auth-Stefanos_A_-Bamopoulos-Aff1-Aff2) et al. 2020)
- msigDB gene sets: GOBP_REGULATION_OF_MRNA_SPLICING_VIA_SPLICEOSOME (M14810), GOBP_ALTERNATIVE_MRNA_SPLICING_VIA_SPLICEOSOME (M10881)

Category 2: Gene sets with clinical/oncogenic relevance

- Custom gene set: [treehouseDruggableGenes_2020-03_25.txt](https://github.com/UCSC-Treehouse/CKCC2/blob/adb997599358916e120f0118e8cffa2cd6bd9890/data/treehouseDruggableGenes_2020-03_25.txt#L4) - Treehouse list of 116 druggable genes used for patient outlier analysis
- msigDB gene sets: HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION (M5930), HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_DN (M5956), HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP (M5953), HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS (M5944), HALLMARK_UV_RESPONSE_DN (M5942), HALLMARK_UV_RESPONSE_UP (M5941)

## Setup

Load libraries

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(msigdbr)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(enrichplot)
```

Define directory and file paths

```{r}
## directories
# repo root
repo_root <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::is_git_root)
# gene sets
gene_set_dir <- file.path(repo_root, "gene_sets")

## files ##
# whole blood vs AML splice results with gene name, median PSI, diffsplice dpsi, and p-adj columns
diffsplice_results_file <- file.path(repo_root, params$in_file)

# gene sets for ORA
treehouse_druggable_genes_file <- file.path(gene_set_dir, "treehouseDruggableGenes_2020-03_25.txt")

# output files
out_ora_file <- file.path(repo_root, params$out_ora_file)
out_sig_diffsplice_file <- file.path(repo_root, params$out_sig_diffsplice_file)
```

Read in files

```{r}
diffsplice_results <- readr::read_tsv(diffsplice_results_file) 
th_druggable_genes <- readr::read_tsv(treehouse_druggable_genes_file)
```

## ORA

Obtain msigdb gene sets relevant to humans

```{r obtain_human_db}
hs_msigdb_df <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens")
```

Define list of genes for custom gene sets and lists of msigDB gene sets of interest

```{r define_gene_lists}
# define custom splice gene list
u2af1_leuk_diffsplice_genes <- c(
  "ABI1",
  "CLTA",
  "DEK",
  "GIT2",
  "HNRNPK",
  "HP1BP3",
  "ITCH",
  "MCM3",
  "NSMAF",
  "PCNXL4",
  "PLEKHM2",
  "PMM2",
  "PPP6R3",
  "RP3-477O4.14",
  "SET",
  "SWI5"
)

# define treehouse druggable gene list
druggable_genes <-th_druggable_genes |> 
  dplyr::pull(gene)

# turn gene lists into data frames
u2af1_leuk_set <- data.frame(
  gs_name = "u2af1_leuk_diffsplice",
  gene_symbol = u2af1_leuk_diffsplice_genes
)

th_druggable_genes_set <- data.frame(
  gs_name = "treehouse_druggable_genes",
  gene_symbol = th_druggable_genes$gene
)

custom_gene_sets <- rbind(u2af1_leuk_set, th_druggable_genes_set)

# filter human msigdb for Hallmark and Oncogenic Signature gene sets 
# change gene set collections here if we decide on different gene sets in the future
filtered_msigdb <- hs_msigdb_df |>
  dplyr::filter(
    gs_collection_name %in% c("Hallmark", "Oncogenic Signature") 
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    gs_name,
    gene_symbol
  )

combined_gene_sets <- rbind(custom_gene_sets, filtered_msigdb)

```

### Retrieve gene lists from splice results for ORA

Background genes (`detected_genes`) are all genes with non-NA (numeric) PSI values quantified for at least min_samples in the reference and query groups. In the test data used here, min_samples is 5.

```{r}
detected_genes <- diffsplice_results |>
  # remove NA p values, as they are present in the diffsplice data frame
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(p_adj)) |>
  # extract gene names column for ORA
  dplyr::pull(gene_names) |>
  # take unique set of parent genes
  unique()
```

Filter for differential splicing results within padj and significance thresholds and obtain the diffsplice gene list

```{r}
# filter for significant diffsplice events
filtered_diffsplice_results <- diffsplice_results |>
  dplyr::filter(
    p_adj < params$padj,
    abs(dPSI) > params$dpsi
  ) |>
  # rank significant diff splice events by abs(dPSI)
  dplyr::arrange(desc(abs(dPSI)))

# obtain vector of significant diffsplice parent genes
diffsplice_genes <- unique(filtered_diffsplice_results$gene_names)
```

### ORA on significantly differentially spliced genes

First, try to perform ORA on the filtered msigdb gene sets. Nothing comes up as significantly enriched, even when using no p value filter.

```{r}
ora_result <- enricher(
  gene = diffsplice_genes, 
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  universe = detected_genes,
  TERM2GENE = combined_gene_sets
)

# check if anything comes up
ora_result |> as.data.frame()
```

## Plot ORA results

Plot overlapping genes in each gene set with an upset plot

```{r}
#| label: fig-upset-plot
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 5

upsetplot(ora_result, n = 10) +
  ggtitle("Overlap of genes in ORA gene sets for AML vs Whole Blood")
```

Plot gene set gene count and significance from ORA: dot plot of gene set gene abundance (gene ratio) and ORA p values

```{r}
#| label: fig-dot-plot
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

dotplot(ora_result)
```

## Write outputs to file

```{r write_output}
readr::write_tsv(as.data.frame(ora_result), out_ora_file)
readr::write_tsv(diffsplice_results, out_sig_diffsplice_file)
```
